questions.question: Can you explain the student enrollment pipeline and how the reference embedding template is generated?
expected_points: Twenty images are captured per student from different angles
Each image is aligned and resized to 160 by 160 pixels
Images are passed through the embedding model and the average embedding is stored as the student template
Raw face images are deleted after enrollment to reduce privacy risk

questions.question: Why did you choose a deep learning embedding approach like FaceNet with MTCNN over earlier methods such as RFID, fingerprints, or Haar cascades?
expected_points: RFID cards allow proxy attendance because cards can be shared
Fingerprint scanners cause queuing since only one student can be scanned at a time
Haar cascades were fast but inaccurate under poor classroom lighting
FaceNet maps faces into a 128-dimensional space with over 99% accuracy on the LFW benchmark and runs in real time on a mid-range GPU

questions.question: How does the system ensure data privacy and secure the storage of biometric data?
expected_points: Face embeddings are stored in a dedicated face_embeddings table encrypted with AES-256
Access to encrypted embeddings is restricted to the API service account
Raw face images are deleted immediately after enrollment
Liveness detection with eye blinking checks prevents spoofing via photos or screens

questions.question: Describe the overall three-tier architecture and how frames are captured and transmitted across the tiers.
expected_points: Capture tier runs on a classroom PC with a 1080p camera sending 1 frame every 2 seconds
Application tier is a Python Flask REST API performing face detection with MTCNN and recognition
Data tier is a MySQL database storing student records, sessions, courses, and attendance

questions.question: How is similarity calculated during recognition, and how did you tune the acceptance threshold?
expected_points: Cosine similarity is calculated between incoming face embeddings and enrolled templates
A threshold of 0.75 was tuned using a validation set of 40 students
At 0.75, it yielded a 0.5% false acceptance rate (FAR) and a 3% false rejection rate (FRR)
The match function returns the student ID with the highest score strictly above 0.75

questions.question: What rule or logic is enforced before a student is officially marked present, and why was it designed this way?
expected_points: A student must be recognized in at least three frames (MIN_FRAMES_FOR_PRESENT = 3)
These frames must occur during the first 15 minutes of the lecture session
This prevents a printed photo held up briefly from being registered as attendance

questions.question: What pilot testing results did you achieve, and did the system satisfy your project's performance objectives?
expected_points: Pilot conducted across 3 classes of 45 students over two weeks
Achieved 96.8% accuracy compared with manual roll call
Marked attendance in an average of 40 seconds per lecture
Successfully met the target of completing attendance in under 1 minute compared to ~10 minutes manual roll calls

questions.question: What were the main sources of recognition errors identified during the pilot, and how did you mitigate them?
expected_points: Errors primarily stemmed from students wearing masks
Errors also occurred for students seated in the back row under poor lighting conditions
Adding a second camera at the back of the room cut these errors by half

questions.question: Explain the database schema design for tracking attendance and how query performance was optimized for reporting.
expected_points: Consists of five main tables: students, courses, enrollments, lecture_sessions, and attendance
The attendance table references student and lecture session, storing first seen time and frame count
Indexes on student_id and session_id keep semester attendance report queries under 100 ms

questions.question: What limitations currently exist in your solution, and what specific future improvements do you propose?
expected_points: Current limitation handling masked faces; future work includes masked face recognition
Developing a mobile application for teachers
Integration with the university learning management system (LMS)
